messages:
Aisha (PM): Heads-up — FinCo just escalated their Dedicated ask. They want guaranteed p99 latency + burstable capacity for peaks. They asked if we can move it up a quarter. 

Luca (Eng): Do we have a concrete SLA target they're expecting? p99 numbers vary by model/seq len.

Aisha (PM): They mentioned p99 < 200ms for text-gen baseline (seq ~256) and ability to burst +20% traffic without manual ops.

Maya (Staff PM): Quick tradeoff thought: we can do a narrow-scope ship that covers 80% of cases (single-model, cached prefix + simple burst routing) vs full autoscale + multi-model support which is 3x dev effort. Which level do we want to commit to?

Raj (Platform Eng): From infra side: narrow ship (routing + soft burst pool) is ~4w of work + config/QA. Full autoscale w/eviction, KV cache persistence, and cross-rack placement is 12w.

Tomasz (SRE): Need to factor in runbook + alerting. If we go narrow we still need canary rollout and automated fallback to hosted models. That’s ~1w SRE effort for runbooks + 1w for canary infra.

Elise (Product Ops): Customer success wants deterministic launch criteria — minimal acceptance: 1) p99 < 200ms on canary for their baseline, 2) documented fallback plan, 3) runbook + oncall rotation for 2 weeks after launch.

Luca (Eng): OK. If we score with RICE-ish thinking: Reach=6 (FinCo + similar mid-market), Impact=8 (revenue + reference), Confidence=6, Effort ~6 (narrow ship -> 6 dev-weeks across teams). RICE-like prioritization favors the narrow ship for Q2.

Aisha (PM): Proposal: commit to Narrow Ship as a time-boxed initiative (Q2). Deliverables: routing + soft-burst pool, prefix caching for the target model, canary + automated fallback to hosted catalog. Post-launch, evaluate full autoscale as follow-up.

Maya (Staff PM): Sounds reasonable. Outstanding deps: eng-infra needs to reallocate 2 engineers for 4w; eng-runtime needs a cache hook change (1 engineer for 2w). Can we get those?

Raj (Platform Eng): We can divert 2 infra engineers by delaying the low-priority HW-migration sprint. I need sign-off from Eng Infra leads.

Luca (Eng): ETA if approved: start of sprint next week -> narrow ship alpha in 4w, canary in week 6.

Tomasz (SRE): I can schedule canary windows and oncall, but we need to lock the rollback policy now. Suggest: automatic weight drop to 0 if error rate > 2% or p99 above 250ms for 3 consecutive min.

Aisha (PM): Agree on rollback thresholds. @Elise — can you own the launch checklist and customer comms?

Elise (Product Ops): I’ll own it. Will draft comms and acceptance checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Maya (Staff PM): One more tradeoff: we can reduce scope further by shipping without prefix cache (less infra work) but that likely misses the p99 target. Risky. 

Luca (Eng): Cache is small work and big payoff for p99 — don't cut it.

Raj (Platform Eng): I’ll circle with infra leads and confirm resource reallocation by EOD. If approved, we’ll create a dedicated team label and adjust the sprint board.

Aisha (PM): Action items: 1) Raj confirm infra resources (EOD) 2) Elise prep checklist & comms (EOD) 3) Luca draft scope doc + risk table (tomorrow morning) 4) Tomasz draft runbook (tomorrow) 5) Aisha to confirm with FinCo on accept criteria and timeline (today).

deploy-bot: Deployed branch feature/dedicated-narrow-ship to staging at 1938771250 :rocket:

Luca (Eng): Nice — that makes testing easier. I’ll start integration tests tonight.

Aisha (PM): Thanks team. If infra confirms we’ll lock this as the Q2 focused initiative. We’ll reconvene in 24h for final decision. :thumbsup:
